purpose: How a home-security dealer turns one household's layout, construction, connectivity, and stated fears into a layered panel/sensor/doorbell/camera design, proves the installation right through workmanship standards, commissioning tests, training, and documented closeout, stays inside licensing, permit, and false-alarm-ordinance obligation classes that must be verified locally, and decides which installs to run in-house versus subcontract without diluting quality or lawful-defensive boundaries.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator is a small residential dealer serving single-family homes and small multi-family units; commercial high-security and certificated commercial fire work are out of scope
low-voltage/alarm licensing, permit, and false-alarm rules differ by state and city; this KB names obligation classes only and every jurisdictional point carries a verify-locally flag
device capabilities are described by class (dual-tech motion, cellular communicator, pet-immune PIR), never by brand benchmark claims or invented specification figures
monitoring exists downstream of this KB; the design-and-install job ends by handing a tested system and clean records to monitoring and service operations
equipment and labor costs are discussed as mechanisms and qualitative bands, never as invented dollar figures stated as fact
exclusions: dealer-program versus independent-model choice, account funding mechanics (equipment subsidy, wholesale/retail monitoring spread, account sale versus hold, holdbacks and chargebacks), territory targeting, and lead generation or in-home selling technique - the acquisition-economics KB owns those

central-station versus self/cloud monitoring stack selection, RMR and service-plan construction, attrition and retention playbooks, renewal practice, and account-book valuation - the monitoring-and-retention KB owns those
any offensive, retaliatory, or covert-surveillance use: no design that monitors occupants without their knowledge, records where privacy is reasonably expected, or targets a neighbor's property
asserting specific state or city licensing, permit, fine, or ordinance rules as fact - this KB names the obligation class and directs the operator to verify current rules in their jurisdiction
stating specific prices, wage rates, fine amounts, or equipment costs as fact - only the mechanism that produces the number and how to verify it per deal
personalized legal, insurance, or financial advice, including promising insurance-premium discounts on the customer's policy
commercial burglary or fire-alarm engineering for banks, jewelers, or code-certificated occupancies beyond recognizing that they demand different credentials and referring them out

competency_questions.question: What must the site survey and risk walk-through capture, on-site and in writing, before any package is designed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SITE_SURVEY_WALKTHROUGH enumerates the physical, household, and existing-equipment facts to record, and CONNECTIVITY_RF_SURVEY adds the cellular and Wi-Fi measurements taken at candidate mount points

competency_questions.question: How does a walk-through become a household threat model that actually drives device selection instead of a generic package?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THREAT_MODEL_FRAMING ranks likely entry paths, folds in the household's stated concerns and prior incidents, and outputs a profile the zone plan consumes

competency_questions.question: How is a layered zone plan built, and why does perimeter detection come before interior motion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LAYERED_ZONE_PLAN states the perimeter-first rule with its detect-before-entry rationale and defines zones, partitions, and entry/exit paths

competency_questions.question: How do I choose the panel platform, sensor bus, and communicator path for a given home, and what lock-in does that choice create?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PANEL_PLATFORM_SELECTION weighs wireless versus hardwired versus hybrid, requires a communicator path proven by connectivity readings, and names the ecosystem lock-in consequence of the choice

competency_questions.question: How are sensor technology and placement matched to construction, pets, sunlight, and HVAC so the system detects intrusion without generating false alarms?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SENSOR_TECH_PLACEMENT maps device class to condition with placement rules, and FALSE_ALARM_ORDINANCE_DESIGN explains why false-alarm exposure disciplines sensitivity choices

competency_questions.question: How do I design camera and doorbell coverage that deters and documents intrusion while staying inside privacy law and the lawful-defensive charter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAMERA_DOORBELL_COVERAGE gives field-of-view, mounting, and masking rules and DEFENSIVE_SECURITY_CHARTER supplies the refusal boundary for covert or privacy-invasive requests

competency_questions.question: When does an existing system get taken over and reused, and when is rip-and-replace the honest recommendation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TAKEOVER_ASSESSMENT gives the component-by-component keep/replace test covering proprietary panels, sensor reuse, communicator swaps, and battery-age evidence

competency_questions.question: What licensing, permit, and alarm-registration obligation classes can attach to a job, and how do I verify what actually applies here before scheduling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSING_AWARENESS_MAP names the license classes with the verify-locally rule, FALSE_ALARM_ORDINANCE_DESIGN covers registration and fine mechanisms, and PERMIT_REGISTRATION_WORKFLOW sequences verification before install

competency_questions.question: What defines an acceptable installation, and how is the whole system proven working before the installer leaves?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INSTALL_WORKMANSHIP_STANDARD defines the checkable workmanship bar and COMMISSIONING_TEST_PROTOCOL requires every zone signal-confirmed end-to-end with the account on test

competency_questions.question: What must customer training and closeout records contain so the household can run the system without false alarms and the office can service it later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CUSTOMER_TRAINING_HANDOFF lists the arming, code, verification-word, and false-alarm behaviors to teach, and CLOSEOUT_RECORDS_HANDOFF defines the as-built record set handed to monitoring and service

competency_questions.question: When should installs be subcontracted versus kept in-house, and how are crews qualified and overseen either way?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBCONTRACT_VS_INHOUSE states the capacity/control trade-off with the licensing-attachment duty, and INSTALLER_VETTING_OVERSIGHT gives the credential, background, and QC oversight regime

competency_questions.question: How do callbacks and false-alarm patterns feed back into design and installation standards instead of being absorbed as one-off truck rolls?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFECT_CALLBACK_LOOP classifies callback root causes and routes each class to the standard it should change

competency_questions.question: What changes when smoke, heat, or CO devices join a monitored security system, and when must the dealer stop and verify credentials before touching fire work?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LIFE_SAFETY_INTEGRATION separates listed supervised life-safety devices from convenience gadgets, names the code and license obligation classes with the verify-locally flag, and defines the refer-out condition

competency_questions.question: What must the written scope proposal disclose honestly about what the system will and will not do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SYSTEM_SCOPE_PROPOSAL requires written inclusions, exclusions, declined coverage, and capability limits, and bans burglar-proof or guaranteed-response claims

glossary.definition: One supervised detection identity on the panel - a contact, motion, glassbreak, or life-safety device (or a defined group of them) with its own name, so the keypad, the central station, and the service tech all know exactly which opening or space tripped.

The design doctrine that doors and reachable windows get contacts and glassbreak coverage before interior motion is added, so intrusion is detected at the shell while the intruder is still outside or entering, with interior devices as the backup layer rather than the only layer.

A motion detector that must see both passive-infrared heat movement and microwave (or similar second-technology) confirmation before tripping; slower to fool by heat drafts or headlights, so it is the standard answer in false-alarm-prone rooms.

The programmed grace window on designated entry zones that lets an authorized person enter and disarm, or arm and leave, without an alarm; every other zone should trip instantly, and over-long delays are a burglar's gift.

The route alarm signals travel to monitoring - today typically a cellular radio as primary with broadband/IP as backup; a path that dies with a cut phone line or a router power loss is a design defect, not bad luck.

Adopting a competitor's or builder's existing installed equipment onto your platform and monitoring instead of ripping it out - viable when the panel or its sensors speak a compatible protocol, hazardous when the incumbent's gear is proprietary, encrypted to their service, or past its service life.

A city or county rule class that typically requires alarm-user registration, escalates fees or fines for repeated false dispatches, and can suspend police response to a chronic address; exact terms vary by jurisdiction and must be verified locally per job.

A policy some jurisdictions adopt under which police respond to burglar alarms only when a human, video, or audio verification indicates a real event; in such territory a contacts-only design is functionally weaker, and the design must include a verification means.

The commissioning exercise of physically tripping every device - opening each door and window, walking each motion pattern, testing each glassbreak with a proper tester - while confirming the panel registers the correct zone each time.

The central-station mode in which an account's incoming signals are logged but not dispatched; placing the account on test before commissioning signal tests is what separates a clean test log from a false police dispatch on install day.

nodes.definition: Hold the bright line that everything this operation designs and installs exists to prevent, detect, and alarm intrusion into the customer's own home - and nothing else. The charter bans covert surveillance of occupants, guests, or workers; cameras or microphones in spaces with a reasonable expectation of privacy (bathrooms, bedrooms of other adults, a tenant's unit); designs aimed at a neighbor's property; and audio capture wherever consent rules make it legally hazardous, which the dealer must verify locally. It also sets the refusal script: when a buyer asks for a hidden camera over the nanny's bed or a lens angled into the neighbor's yard, the dealer declines, explains the lawful alternative (disclosed cameras, exterior coverage of their own approach paths), and walks away if the buyer insists.

included: refusal script for covert or targeting requests
excluded: general privacy-law advice to the customer
camera aiming mechanics, which the camera design node owns

pros.claim: A stated charter lets any installer refuse a bad request on the spot without negotiating ethics door by door
pros.example: a tech declines a concealed bedroom camera aimed at a caregiver by citing company policy instead of arguing law from memory

cons.claim: Bright-line refusals cost real revenue from buyers who will simply hire a looser competitor
cons.example: losing a full camera package sale because the buyer insisted one lens cover the neighbor's driveway

failure_modes: installing a covert interior camera because the homeowner signed a waiver, which does not cure the occupant's privacy interest
treating audio recording as a free camera feature when local consent rules make it the riskiest channel in the house
acceptance_tests: every camera and microphone in the design names its purpose, its disclosed status, and passes the defensive-purpose test, and every refused request is logged with the alternative offered
revisit_triggers: a recording-consent or surveillance statute changes in a served jurisdiction
a request pattern emerges that the current refusal script does not cleanly cover

base.update_signal: a privacy or consent law change, or a customer-request pattern that tests the covert-surveillance boundary

nodes.definition: Know which credential classes can govern this trade and verify which apply before working: many states license alarm companies and their agents (often with fingerprinting and background checks), separately license low-voltage electrical work, and sometimes carve out a distinct fire-alarm class; some cities add their own contractor registration on top. The map is held as obligation classes - company license, individual agent card, low-voltage specialty, fire endorsement, local registration - each with a per-jurisdiction verification step, because asserting a remembered rule is how a dealer installs illegally in the next county over. The node also fixes who must hold the credential when subcontractors do the work, since a licensed dealer using unlicensed subs is a classic enforcement target.

included: credential obligation classes for alarm and low-voltage work
who must hold the license when subs install
excluded: asserting any state or city's current rule as fact
per-job permit paperwork, which the permit workflow node owns

pros.claim: Holding the rules as classes plus a verification step travels across jurisdictions without going stale
pros.example: expanding into a neighboring city triggers a checklist lookup of its registration and permit posture instead of assuming home-county rules apply

cons.claim: Per-jurisdiction verification adds friction and delay to every out-of-area job
cons.example: a single install two towns over requiring an afternoon of licensing-board and city-clerk checks before it can be quoted honestly

failure_modes: quoting fire-alarm work under a burglar-alarm credential in a state that separates the two classes
assuming the company license covers individual installers where agent registration is separately required
acceptance_tests: every job file names the jurisdiction, the credential classes checked, the verification date and source, and the credential holder covering the work
revisit_triggers: a served state or city changes its licensing classes or enforcement posture
the operation enters a new jurisdiction or adds a new work type such as monitored fire

base.update_signal: a licensing-class change in a served jurisdiction or entry into a new one

nodes.definition: Treat the local false-alarm regime as a design input, not an after-sale surprise. The obligation class: many cities require the alarm user to register or permit the system, charge escalating fees or fines after a small number of false dispatches, and can put a chronic address on no-response status; a minority run verified-response policies where police come only on confirmed events. Exact registration triggers, fee ladders, and response policies vary block by block and must be verified per job. Designing under this regime means favoring confirmation-friendly layouts (dual-tech motion where pets roam, cross-zoning options, video that lets monitoring verify), realistic entry delays, and telling the customer plainly that their city fines repeat false alarms and how the system and their habits prevent that.

included: design and disclosure choices that reduce false-dispatch exposure
excluded: quoting any city's actual fee ladder as fact
the registration paperwork itself, which the permit workflow node executes

pros.claim: Designing against the ordinance up front protects the customer relationship the whole account depends on
pros.example: specifying pet-immune dual-tech in a three-dog household so the new owner's first month brings zero fined dispatches

cons.claim: Confirmation-biased design can under-alarm real events at the margin
cons.example: a cross-zoned interior that stays silent when a single sensor sees a real intruder for only a moment

failure_modes: selling a system in a verified-response city without any verification means, leaving the customer with alarms police ignore
never mentioning registration duties so the customer's first contact with their ordinance is a fine
acceptance_tests: each job records the jurisdiction's registration duty, response policy, and fine mechanism as verified on a stated date, and the design notes which features exist to limit false-dispatch exposure
revisit_triggers: a served city changes its response policy or fine structure
false-dispatch reports climb for installs in one jurisdiction

base.update_signal: an ordinance, fee, or response-policy change in a served city, or a false-dispatch cluster there

nodes.definition: Walk the property with the customer and record what the design will stand on: every exterior door and its construction, every ground-reachable or ladder-reachable window, sliders and pet doors, garage and interior garage door, sightlines and dark approaches, fence lines and gate habits, floor plan and stair layout, where people sleep, who holds keys, pets and their roaming range, existing wiring and any legacy equipment, panel and keypad candidate locations near power and egress paths, and the household's daily arm/disarm rhythm. The survey is a written, photographed artifact - not a mental note - because the designer, the proposal writer, and the installer may be three different people on three different days, and every fact that lives only in the surveyor's head becomes a change order later.

included: household patterns, pets, and prior incidents
excluded: signal measurements, which the connectivity survey owns
device selection, which design nodes own

pros.claim: A written, photographed survey lets design and install proceed without re-visiting the home
pros.example: the installer pre-cuts wire lengths and picks mounts from survey photos instead of discovering a brick exterior on install morning

cons.claim: A thorough walk-through consumes unbilled hours on prospects who may never sign
cons.example: an hour-long survey plus write-up for a homeowner who was only fishing for a price to negotiate elsewhere

failure_modes: surveying only the front of the house and missing the alley-facing basement window burglars actually use
failing to record the dogs, so the design ships standard-sensitivity motions into a false-alarm factory
acceptance_tests: the survey record lists every exterior opening with construction type, all pets, prior incidents, existing equipment, and panel/keypad candidates, each backed by a photo
revisit_triggers: a renovation, move, or new pet changes the surveyed facts before install
install-day discoveries contradict the survey record

base.update_signal: install-day contradictions of the survey or a change at the home between survey and install

nodes.definition: Measure, during the same visit, whether signals will actually work where devices will actually go: cellular signal strength at the panel's candidate wall (the communicator lives or dies there), Wi-Fi throughput at each camera and doorbell position rather than beside the router, the router's capacity and upload headroom for however many video streams the design contemplates, and the wireless-sensor propagation obstacles the construction implies - metal lath under old stucco, foil-backed insulation, long runs to a detached garage. Readings are recorded per location because 'the house has good service' is a sales sentence, while 'two bars at the northeast utility wall, panel moved to the hallway closet' is an engineering fact the platform choice depends on.

excluded: choosing the platform, which the panel node owns
camera count and aiming, which the camera node owns

pros.claim: Per-location readings prevent the worst install-day failure, a communicator that cannot report
pros.example: moving the panel from the dead-zone garage wall to an interior closet because the survey showed no usable cellular at the original spot

cons.claim: Point-in-time readings can flatter conditions that degrade later
cons.example: a summer Wi-Fi reading that collapses in winter when the family's evening streaming saturates the uplink the cameras share

failure_modes: testing Wi-Fi next to the router and mounting the camera three walls away
skipping the cellular check because the installer's own phone had bars in the driveway
acceptance_tests: the readings sheet shows cellular strength at the chosen panel location and Wi-Fi results at every planned camera position, each tied to the spot where the device will mount
revisit_triggers: commissioning signal tests fail or run marginal at any device
the customer changes internet provider or router before install

base.update_signal: a failed or marginal commissioning signal test, or a change to the home's internet service

nodes.definition: When the home already has a system, judge component by component whether to adopt it or replace it. Wired contacts and sirens in good condition are often the best free asset in the house; the incumbent panel is the usual casualty because many are proprietary, locked to the prior company's service, or running an installer code nobody will surrender. The test per component: does it speak a protocol the new platform supports, is it within service life (sensor batteries, siren drivers, backup battery age), can it be tested to prove function, and does reusing it save real labor versus the risk of inheriting an undocumented fault. The verdict is written and honest - including telling a customer their beloved twenty-year-old panel is the one thing that must go, and why - because a takeover that limps is a service burden the operation carries for years.

excluded: the incumbent's contract or monitoring obligations, which the sibling KBs own
new-device selection, which design nodes own

pros.claim: Reusing sound wired infrastructure cuts install labor and wall damage dramatically
pros.example: adopting a builder-wired home's door contacts and siren run, so the install is a panel swap plus programming instead of a whole-house pull

cons.claim: Inherited equipment carries undocumented history the new operation now owns
cons.example: a reused attic siren that fails its first real alarm because a rodent-chewed run was never in any record

failure_modes: promising a takeover before discovering the incumbent panel is locked and its sensors are encrypted to that vendor
reusing every legacy sensor untested to keep the quote low, then eating the service calls
acceptance_tests: every legacy component has a written keep/replace verdict with its compatibility evidence and test result, or the file records that no usable equipment exists
revisit_triggers: commissioning reveals a reused component failing its test
a takeover-heavy install pattern starts showing elevated callback rates

base.update_signal: a reused component failing under test or in service, or a platform change that alters takeover compatibility

nodes.definition: Convert the walk-through into a ranked statement of what this specific household is defending against. Residential burglary overwhelmingly favors the easy entries - doors, ground-floor and slider glass, the attached garage - so those rank first by default, adjusted by what the survey saw: the dark side yard, the alley window, the ladder left by the shed. Onto that spine go the household's own concerns, taken seriously and weighed honestly - a prior break-in through a specific window, package theft at the porch, a family member's medical event, wildfire or freeze exposure for environmental add-ons - and the constraint set: pets, small children, elderly users, rental status. The output is a short profile that names the top entry paths, the priority assets and people, and the customer's stated fears, so the zone plan is an answer to this home rather than a brochure package with the address changed.

included: constraint set for design (pets, users, tenancy)
excluded: fear-based exaggeration of risk, banned by the ethics rules
device selection, which the design nodes own

pros.claim: A per-home threat model justifies every device in plain language the customer can echo
pros.example: explaining that the slider gets a contact plus glassbreak because it is the hidden, pry-friendly entry the walk-through flagged

cons.claim: Customer fears can dominate the model and misallocate budget away from actual weak points
cons.example: a buyer fixated on front-door cameras while the unlit rear slider - the likelier entry - goes uncovered

failure_modes: shipping the same three-door-two-motion default into every home regardless of what the survey found
inflating the threat picture to upsell, which is fear-selling and breaks the ethics boundary
acceptance_tests: the profile ranks entry paths with survey evidence, records the household's stated concerns and constraints, and every later device traces to a line in it
revisit_triggers: a neighborhood incident or household change alters the risk picture
the customer declines coverage on a top-ranked entry path, which the proposal must then record

base.update_signal: a household or neighborhood change that shifts the ranked entry paths or the constraint set

nodes.definition: Lay out the detection architecture as layers with the perimeter first: contacts on every exterior door and the reachable operable windows, glassbreak coverage for the vulnerable panes, then interior motion as the backup net covering the paths an intruder must cross - stairs, hallway pinch points, the room with the safe - and finally 24-hour zones (life-safety, panics, environmental) that never disarm. Each zone gets a distinct, human-readable identity so a signal names the actual opening, and entry/exit delay is granted only to the doors the family genuinely uses, with everything else instant. The plan also decides partitioning where the home needs it - a detached shop, an in-law unit armed on its own schedule - and reflects the false-alarm regime, since a plan that leans on hair-trigger interior motion in a fined city is a liability dressed as coverage.

excluded: which device model fills each zone, owned by sensor selection
camera placement, owned by the camera node

pros.claim: Perimeter-first catches the intruder at the shell, before they are inside with the family
pros.example: a pried back door trips its contact at the frame instead of waiting for a hallway motion to see someone already indoors

cons.claim: Full perimeter coverage multiplies device count and cost on window-heavy homes
cons.example: a 1920s bungalow with eighteen operable windows where contacts-everywhere doubles the equipment budget against a motion-centric design

failure_modes: granting entry delay to every door so a burglar through the side door gets a silent half-minute head start
generic zone names like the panel's default numbering, turning every alarm and service call into a guessing game
acceptance_tests: every ranked entry path from the threat profile is covered by a perimeter-layer device, every zone carries a location-true name, and only designated entry doors have delay
revisit_triggers: the threat profile changes or the customer declines part of the perimeter layer
false-alarm or missed-detection patterns implicate the layering choices

base.update_signal: a coverage gap found in commissioning or service, or a threat-profile change that re-ranks entry paths

nodes.definition: Choose the brain the whole account will live on: wireless, hardwired, or hybrid panel architecture matched to the home's construction and the takeover verdict; a sensor ecosystem whose device catalog covers what the zone plan needs; and a communicator path - cellular primary with IP backup as the modern default - proven viable by the connectivity readings at the actual panel location. The choice is a commitment: the platform fixes which sensors and cameras integrate cleanly, what the monitoring side can receive, and how painful the operation's own future service and takeovers become, so ecosystem lock-in is weighed deliberately rather than discovered later. Panel placement itself is part of the decision - reachable for service, near power, on the entry path for keypad use, not in the first room a burglar reaches to smash before the delay expires, which is why a separated keypad-plus-hidden-panel layout often wins.

included: ecosystem catalog fit and lock-in weighing
excluded: monitoring-stack and central-station selection, owned by the monitoring KB
per-zone device models, owned by sensor selection

pros.claim: One deliberate platform standard across the install base compounds into faster installs and cheaper service
pros.example: techs who program the same panel family daily finish a takeover in half the time they would on a one-off exotic platform

cons.claim: Platform commitment concentrates risk in one vendor's pricing, quality, and end-of-life decisions
cons.example: a radio-generation sunset forcing communicator swap visits across every account on the standardized platform

failure_modes: choosing the platform by habit and discovering its catalog lacks the shock sensors the zone plan specified
mounting the panel beside the front door where a smash-and-grab kills it inside the entry delay
acceptance_tests: the decision record shows the architecture choice justified against construction and takeover evidence, a communicator path backed by the readings sheet, and a panel location argued for service access and smash resistance
revisit_triggers: a vendor announces a radio sunset, price restructure, or catalog gap that touches the standard platform
commissioning or service data shows communicator failures on the chosen path

base.update_signal: a vendor sunset, catalog, or reliability change on the standard platform, or repeated communicator-path failures

nodes.definition: Fill each zone with the device class and mounting that fits the real conditions: recessed versus surface contacts by door material and sightline, wide-gap contacts on rattly old frames, shock or glassbreak sensors placed within acoustic range of the panes they guard and away from noise-alike sources, pet-immune or dual-technology motion mounted at the height and angle that watches human paths while ignoring the dog's, and environmental devices - water at the heater and laundry, low-temperature where pipes freeze - as the quiet add-ons that save more money than the burglar gear. Placement discipline carries the load: a perfect sensor aimed at a sun-heated window wall, an HVAC vent, or the ceiling fan is a false-alarm generator, and the false-alarm regime makes every such mistake a billable insult to the customer.

included: mount height, angle, and acoustic-range rules
excluded: camera and doorbell devices, owned by the camera node
zone architecture, owned by the zone plan

pros.claim: Condition-matched devices deliver detection the household never has to fight
pros.example: a dual-tech motion mounted high in the pet corridor that catches a human crossing at night and ignores two labradors for years

cons.claim: Specialty devices cost more per point and lengthen the design against a bare-bones competitor quote
cons.example: wide-gap and recessed contacts across an old farmhouse pricing visibly above a rival's stick-on-everything bid

failure_modes: standard motion at knee height in a cat household, tripping nightly until the customer stops arming the system
glassbreak mounted around a corner from the pane it nominally guards, deaf to the actual break
acceptance_tests: each zone's record names the device class, its mount position, and the surveyed condition that dictated the choice, and every motion in a pet home is pet-rated or placed out of the pet's plane
revisit_triggers: false-alarm or missed-event reports cluster on a device class or placement pattern
the platform's device catalog changes what classes are available

base.update_signal: a false-alarm cluster tied to a device class or placement, or a catalog change on the platform

nodes.definition: Design the video layer to see what matters and nothing it must not: doorbell on the primary approach (with its power path - existing chime transformer, new transformer, or battery cadence - decided up front), cameras on driveway, entries, and the dark sides the survey flagged, mounted high enough to resist tampering but angled to catch faces rather than hat tops, with night performance and eave power runs planned rather than improvised. Privacy is engineered in: fields of view stay on the customer's own property, masking zones blank the neighbor's windows and yard where the lens cannot avoid them, interior cameras live only in common spaces with every adult occupant aware, and audio features are enabled only where consent rules - verified locally - permit. Bandwidth honesty closes the node: each camera's upload demand is checked against the measured Wi-Fi and the router's headroom, because a stuttering, offline camera is the most-complained-about device in the industry.

excluded: cloud-video plan pricing and monitoring integration economics, owned by the monitoring KB
covert or neighbor-targeting placements, banned by the charter

pros.claim: Well-aimed video both deters and gives monitoring the verification that gets police response in skeptical jurisdictions
pros.example: a driveway camera whose clip of a prowler at the side gate turns a would-be ignored alarm into a verified dispatch

cons.claim: Every camera adds recurring bandwidth, storage, and privacy surface the household must live with
cons.example: a four-camera package that saturates a rural DSL uplink, knocking the family's video calls offline every motion event

failure_modes: aiming a floodlight camera across the fence into the neighbor's kitchen and turning the install into a dispute
doorbell mounted on the trim where the sun blinds it exactly at delivery hour
acceptance_tests: every camera's planned field of view is sketched and checked against the charter with masking noted, each camera's upload demand fits the measured connection, and the doorbell's power path is specified
revisit_triggers: a privacy complaint or consent-rule change touches any installed view
camera-offline or clip-quality complaints trace to bandwidth or placement

base.update_signal: a privacy dispute, a consent-law change, or a pattern of bandwidth-driven camera complaints

nodes.definition: Treat monitored smoke, heat, and CO as a different class of work grafted onto the security system, not another gadget on the list. Monitored life-safety devices must be listed for the purpose, supervised on 24-hour zones that no arming state silences, and placed with code intent - sleeping areas, each level, the mechanical spaces - while respecting that residential fire-alarm requirements and who may legally install them are code and license questions that vary by jurisdiction and must be verified before quoting, since some places reserve interconnected or fire-code work for a separate credential class. The dealer's honest lane: add listed monitored detectors where permitted, never remove or degrade the home's existing code-required detection, escalate fire signals with the priority monitoring assigns them, and refer out anything that crosses into fire-code territory the operation is not credentialed for. Done right this is the highest-value save in the catalog - the account that detects the 2 a.m. garage fire pays for every system the dealer ever installs.

included: placement with code intent and verify-locally duty
excluded: certificated commercial fire systems
asserting any jurisdiction's fire code as fact

pros.claim: Monitored life-safety protects the household when nobody is home to hear a standalone beep
pros.example: a monitored heat detector in the garage reporting a car fire at 2 a.m. while the family sleeps upstairs behind closed doors

cons.claim: Life-safety raises the stakes of every shortcut far beyond burglary gear
cons.example: an unsupervised smoke zone that dies silently and is discovered only when the detector fails to report a real fire

failure_modes: quoting monitored fire work in a jurisdiction that reserves it for a credential class the operation lacks
putting a smoke detector on a normal burglary zone that the customer's disarm silences
acceptance_tests: every life-safety device is listed for its purpose, sits on a supervised 24-hour zone, has its jurisdictional permissibility verified and recorded, and existing code-required detection is left intact
revisit_triggers: a fire-code or licensing change in a served jurisdiction
a supervision or signal failure on any life-safety zone in the field

base.update_signal: a fire-code or credential-class change, or any field failure on a life-safety zone

nodes.definition: Reduce the design to a written scope the customer can hold the operation to: the bill of materials by zone, the labor scope including wall repair and cleanup expectations, what is expressly excluded, how change orders will be priced when the walls reveal surprises, and - the honesty core - what the system will not do. No system prevents all burglary; response times belong to police and monitoring, not to the dealer's promises; cameras deter and document but do not physically stop anyone. Declined coverage gets its own line: when the customer refuses contacts on the vulnerable rear slider to save money, that refusal is recorded in the proposal they sign, protecting both sides and keeping the trim visible instead of silent. Equipment and labor pricing appears as this job's actual quote built from its parts list and hours - the mechanism - never dressed up with invented market-rate claims.

included: labor scope, exclusions, and change-order terms
written capability limits and no-overpromise rule
excluded: monitoring contract terms, auto-renewal, and cancellation language, owned by the monitoring KB
financing and subsidy structures, owned by the economics KB

pros.claim: A written scope with limits converts install-day disputes into document lookups
pros.example: the customer who expected the detached shed covered reads the exclusions line they initialed instead of demanding free devices

cons.claim: Explicit limits and exclusions read as hedging against a competitor's confident vagueness
cons.example: losing a signature to a rival whose one-page quote promises total protection with no exclusions list

failure_modes: selling protection language a system cannot deliver, which surfaces as fraud claims after the first loss
trimming the quote to win the deal and leaving the removed coverage undocumented
acceptance_tests: the signed scope lists every device by zone, states exclusions and change-order terms, contains no prevention or response guarantee, and records any declined coverage with the customer's initials
revisit_triggers: install-day discoveries force a change order
a dispute or complaint pattern traces to proposal language

base.update_signal: a dispute pattern tied to scope language or recurring change orders from survey-to-proposal gaps

nodes.definition: Execute the jurisdictional paperwork the frame nodes flagged, in the right order: verify current requirements with the actual authorities (city or county permit office, alarm-administration program, licensing board where relevant) rather than from memory; pull any required electrical or low-voltage permit before the drills come out; register the alarm user with the local false-alarm program before or at activation so the first dispatch is not from an unregistered address; and file the evidence - permit numbers, registration confirmations, inspection sign-offs where demanded - into the job record. Where a jurisdiction requires nothing, that finding is documented with its date and source, because 'not required' asserted from habit and 'verified not required on this date from this office' are different facts, and only one of them survives an enforcement letter.

included: per-job verification with the actual authority
alarm registration before or at activation
excluded: knowing every jurisdiction's rules by heart, replaced by the verification duty
licensing-class strategy, owned by the licensing map

pros.claim: Paper in the file before work starts turns inspections and enforcement contacts into non-events
pros.example: an inspector's surprise visit answered by handing over the permit and the registration confirmation from the job folder

cons.claim: Permit cycles put jurisdiction-speed delays into the install calendar
cons.example: a two-week permit backlog idling a crew while the customer asks daily why the boxes are sitting in their garage

failure_modes: activating monitoring on an unregistered address so the customer's first false alarm arrives with a fine and a lecture
letting a sub pull no permit on the assumption the dealer's license covers it
acceptance_tests: the job file holds, before commissioning, either the required permits and registration confirmations or a dated, sourced not-required finding for each obligation class
revisit_triggers: an authority changes its permit or registration process
an enforcement contact or failed inspection on any job

base.update_signal: a process change at any served authority, or an enforcement or inspection failure

nodes.definition: Decide, as a standing policy revisited by volume, which installs the operation performs with employees and which it subcontracts. In-house crews carry the culture, the workmanship standard, and the customer relationship, but cap throughput at payroll size and turn idle weeks into fixed cost; sub crews scale with demand and bring specialty skills (lift work, structured cabling), but rent their loyalty by the job, tempt scope-cutting on piece rates, and drag the dealer's license and reputation into every corner they cut. The trade-off is governed, not felt: licensing must attach correctly to sub work (whose credential covers it - verify per jurisdiction), insurance certificates current, piece-rate structures shaped so tested-and-documented is what gets paid, and the sub decision biased in-house for complex takeovers and life-safety work where judgment matters most.

included: in-house versus sub decision policy by job type and volume
licensing and insurance attachment for sub work
excluded: individual crew vetting mechanics, owned by the vetting node
hiring and payroll administration

pros.claim: Sub capacity absorbs demand spikes without carrying payroll through the troughs
pros.example: a builder handing over a twelve-home closing month that two employee techs could never cover alone

cons.claim: Piece-rate subs inherit every incentive to skip what the customer cannot see
cons.example: a sub crew leaving zone labels and walk tests undone because the rate pays per completed house, not per verified zone

failure_modes: scaling into sub-heavy installs faster than QC can inspect them, so the callback wave arrives a quarter later
sub work performed outside the license attachment the jurisdiction requires
acceptance_tests: a written routing policy says which job classes may be subbed, every active sub has verified license attachment and current insurance on file, and sub pay is tied to passed QC rather than raw completions
revisit_triggers: volume shifts that idle employees or overload them
callback or QC data diverging between sub and in-house installs

base.update_signal: a volume swing, a sub-quality divergence in QC data, or a licensing-attachment change for sub work

nodes.definition: Qualify and continuously oversee everyone the operation sends into a customer's home, employee or sub. Entry bar: whatever agent registration or license card the jurisdiction requires (verify locally), a background check proportionate to the trust being granted - these people learn alarm codes, floor plans, and when the family is away - and demonstrated competence on the platform before solo work. Ongoing oversight: ride-alongs for new crews, photo-documented QC inspection of completed jobs on a sampling schedule that tightens for new or slipping crews, per-crew callback and false-alarm tracking, and a revocation path that actually removes a failing crew instead of quietly re-booking around them. The customer let the operation into their home on trust; the vetting regime is what makes that trust a process rather than a hope.

included: sampled QC inspection and per-crew metrics
excluded: the sub-versus-employee routing policy, owned by the capacity node
general HR policy beyond install-trust roles

pros.claim: Per-crew quality metrics find the slipping installer while the damage is still small
pros.example: one crew's rising thirty-day callback rate triggering re-inspection of their recent jobs before the pattern reaches fifty homes

cons.claim: A high entry bar shrinks the available crew pool exactly when capacity is scarcest
cons.example: turning away two willing sub crews in a busy season because neither could show the required agent cards

failure_modes: skipping the background check for a referred crew because the referral felt like vouching
QC sampling that quietly stops during busy months, which is when quality actually slips
acceptance_tests: every active installer's file shows the jurisdiction-required credential, a completed background check, and platform sign-off, and QC inspection records exist at the declared sampling rate for every crew
revisit_triggers: a crew's callback or QC-failure rate crosses the flag threshold
a jurisdiction changes its agent registration requirements

base.update_signal: a crew metric crossing its flag threshold or an agent-registration rule change

nodes.definition: Define what a finished install physically looks like, in checkable terms: wire runs concealed or raceway-dressed, penetrations sealed against weather and pests, devices mounted level and torqued to their surface (masonry anchors in brick, no drywall-screw shortcuts on sirens), every zone and wire labeled to match the zone schedule, tamper switches enabled, panel backup battery installed and dated, the doorbell transformer's work done to code, and the site left clean enough that the only evidence of the visit is the equipment. The standard exists as a photo-documented QC checklist filled on every job - not an oral tradition - so a second person can verify workmanship from the record, sub crews are held to the identical bar as employees, and the punch list must be empty before the job may proceed to commissioning.

included: physical workmanship rules for routing, mounting, sealing, labeling
excluded: functional signal testing, owned by commissioning
who performs the work, owned by capacity and vetting nodes

pros.claim: A checkable standard makes quality inspectable by someone other than the person who did the work
pros.example: an office review catching an unsealed exterior penetration from the QC photos before the customer finds it with the first rain

cons.claim: Checklist discipline adds visible time to every job and reads as bureaucracy to veteran techs
cons.example: a twenty-year installer bristling at photographing wire dress he has done correctly for decades

failure_modes: unlabeled zones that turn every future service call into re-discovery of the installer's choices
cosmetic shortcuts in crawl spaces and attics where the customer will never look but moisture and rodents will
acceptance_tests: every completed job has its QC checklist with photos, zone labels matching the schedule, dated backup battery, and an empty punch list signed before commissioning
revisit_triggers: callback root causes implicate a workmanship rule or its enforcement
a new device class or construction type needs rules the checklist lacks

base.update_signal: a callback pattern tracing to a workmanship rule, or a new device or construction class entering the catalog

nodes.definition: Prove the system works end to end before anyone calls it installed. With the account placed on test at the central station, walk-test every device - open every contacted door and window, walk every motion's pattern, test each glassbreak with a proper tester, trip each life-safety device by its approved test method - and confirm at the monitoring side that each signal arrived on the correct zone with the correct label. Then exercise the communicator: primary path signal, backup path signal with the primary deliberately failed, panel behavior on AC loss and on battery. Entry and exit delays are timed against the programmed values, keypads and user codes verified, and the whole run is captured in a commissioning log listing each zone, its test result, and the received-at-monitoring confirmation. A zone that cannot be proven received is an open defect, and the job does not hand off around it.

included: on-test walk test of every device
commissioning log as the gate artifact
excluded: monitoring response procedures after handoff, owned by the monitoring KB
workmanship items, owned by the install standard

pros.claim: Per-zone received-signal confirmation is the only proof the system protects rather than merely exists
pros.example: a walk test exposing a garage contact that chimes locally but never reaches monitoring because its zone was mistyped as local-only

cons.claim: Full commissioning holds expensive labor on-site after the visible work is done
cons.example: a two-tech crew spending the day's last hour walking zones and phoning the central station while the next job waits

failure_modes: testing signals without the account on test, dispatching police to the install
sampling a few zones instead of all and shipping the one mis-programmed contact untested
acceptance_tests: the commissioning log shows every zone walk-tested with a received-at-monitoring confirmation, both communicator paths exercised, power-loss behavior verified, and delays timed to programmed values
revisit_triggers: any zone fails or tests marginal at commissioning
field incidents reveal a failure class the protocol does not currently exercise

base.update_signal: a commissioning failure, or a field incident exposing an untested failure class

nodes.definition: Teach the household to run the system before the crew leaves, because an untrained customer is the leading false-alarm source and the fastest route to a resented system that never gets armed. The session covers arming modes and when to use each (stay versus away, what bypassing means), every user's own code and why codes are not shared with the babysitter's whole family, the verification word and what the monitoring call will sound like so a startled customer does not hang up on the operator, how to cancel an accidental alarm before dispatch, pet and houseguest realities, doorbell and app basics, and the jurisdiction's false-alarm consequences in plain terms. Each adult user demonstrates arm, disarm, and cancel at least once; leaflets do not count as training. The session closes with the test-it-monthly habit and who to call for service, and the sign-off records who was trained on what.

included: arming modes, codes, cancel and verification-word practice
excluded: contract, billing, and renewal conversations, owned by the sibling KBs
monitoring's own operator procedures

pros.claim: Hands-on practice at handoff prevents the panic false alarms of the first month
pros.example: a grandmother who rehearsed the cancel sequence calmly stopping a dispatch after the cat tripped a hallway motion

cons.claim: Training lands at the day's end when both crew and customer want to be done, so it erodes first under schedule pressure
cons.example: a crew running late compressing training to an app download and a pamphlet, and that house generating three false alarms in week one

failure_modes: training only the purchasing spouse while the rest of the household learns by triggering alarms
skipping the verification-word explanation so the customer hangs up on the monitoring call as a scam
acceptance_tests: the sign-off shows each adult user demonstrated arm, disarm, and cancel, received their own code, and was briefed on the verification word and local false-alarm consequences
revisit_triggers: early-life false alarms cluster on user error
the household composition or the app interface changes materially

base.update_signal: user-error false alarms in the first months, or an interface change that invalidates the taught flow

nodes.definition: Close the job by writing down what was actually built, because the install crew's memory is not a service plan. The closeout package: the as-built zone schedule (every zone, device class, and location as installed, including install-day deviations from the design), QC and commissioning logs, equipment models and serials with warranty start dates, permit and registration numbers, panel access notes short of anything that would compromise the customer, photos of concealed work before walls closed, and the training sign-off. This package is the handoff artifact to monitoring and service operations - the boundary where this KB's job ends - and its quality is what a future tech stands on when a zone faults at 3 a.m. three years from now. A job is not done when the customer waves goodbye; it is done when the record set is filed and retrievable.

included: test, permit, warranty, and training records
excluded: monitoring account administration and service-plan content, owned by the monitoring KB
storing customer secrets beyond what service requires

pros.claim: A complete as-built lets any future tech service the system without archaeology
pros.example: a zone-fault call three years on resolved in one visit because the record named the device, its location, and the wire path behind the den wall

cons.claim: Closeout paperwork competes with the next billable job and loses when nobody enforces it
cons.example: a busy month of installs closed as done with empty record folders, discovered when the first service calls arrive

failure_modes: as-builts that describe the design rather than the install-day reality with its field changes
records scattered across a tech's phone photos and glovebox instead of a retrievable file
acceptance_tests: the filed package contains the as-built zone schedule with deviations noted, commissioning and QC logs, permit and registration numbers, serials with warranty dates, and the training sign-off, retrievable by job identifier
revisit_triggers: a service call is impeded by a missing or wrong record
the monitoring or service side requests fields the package does not carry

base.update_signal: a service call blocked by record gaps, or a changed downstream field requirement

nodes.definition: Treat every callback, early-life failure, and false alarm as data about the process, not just a truck roll to absorb. Each event gets a root-cause class: user error (training defect), placement or device-class error (design defect), physical failure (workmanship or component defect), programming error (commissioning defect), or environmental change at the home. Classes are tracked per crew, per device class, and per jurisdiction, and each class routes to the standard it should change - a cluster of pet-tripped motions rewrites the placement rule, a crew's loose-mount pattern tightens their QC sampling, a rash of user-error alarms rebuilds the training script. The loop closes only when the changed standard demonstrably bends the curve; a callback rate that stays flat after the fix means the root cause was misdiagnosed. This discipline is also the operation's honest early-warning system for the attrition the monitoring side will otherwise inherit.

included: root-cause classification of callbacks and false alarms
routing each class to the standard it changes
verifying the fix bends the curve
excluded: retention and cancellation-save playbooks, owned by the monitoring KB
warranty cost accounting

pros.claim: Root-caused callbacks convert service pain into permanent standard upgrades
pros.example: three water-heater-closet motion falses in one quarter producing a placement rule that ends the class for good

cons.claim: Classification discipline is overhead that busy seasons quietly abandon
cons.example: a summer backlog of callbacks all closed as fixed with no class recorded, leaving winter's standards no smarter

failure_modes: fixing each symptom at the house while the same defect ships in every new install
blaming users by default, which hides design and placement defects behind a training excuse
acceptance_tests: every callback record carries a root-cause class and the standard it was routed to, and quarterly review shows callback and false-alarm rates per class with the fixes' observed effect
revisit_triggers: a class's rate fails to fall after its standard was changed
a new failure class appears that the taxonomy does not cover

base.update_signal: a callback class rate that resists its fix, or a novel failure class outside the taxonomy

edges.why_related: the threat model is synthesized from the openings, sightlines, and household facts the walk-through recorded
signal readings are taken at the candidate mount points the walk-through identified
the takeover verdict starts from the legacy equipment inventory the survey captured
the zone plan exists to cover the entry paths and assets the threat profile ranked
the local false-alarm regime disciplines how much the plan may lean on trigger-happy interior coverage
the communicator path and wireless architecture are only viable where the readings say they are
which legacy components survive dictates what the new platform must speak
device selection fills the zones the plan defined; without the plan there is nothing to fill
the platform's catalog bounds which device classes can be specified per zone
video coverage is planned against the same ranked entries and dark approaches the zone plan encodes
life-safety devices must be listed and supervised on the chosen panel's 24-hour zones
the proposal's bill of materials is the priced projection of the device schedule
the camera plan's device list and its disclosed limits flow into the written scope
life-safety inclusions, their verified permissibility, and any refer-out must appear in the signed scope
the permit workflow executes the obligation classes the licensing map identified for this jurisdiction
alarm-user registration with the local program is the ordinance node's paperwork made real
permits are pulled against the signed scope's actual work content, not the draft design
the routing policy decides who installs; vetting then qualifies and oversees exactly those crews
the install executes the signed scope; workmanship is judged against what the customer bought
the QC checklist is enforced through the oversight regime that inspects and scores crews
commissioning tests a physically finished install; an open punch list invalidates the test run
the commissioning log is the spine of the closeout package handed to monitoring and service
callback root-causing needs the as-built and test records to tell defect from deviation
every field of view, interior placement, and audio feature must pass the charter's defensive-purpose and privacy tests
edges.risk_of_conflict: coverage ambitions creep across property lines and into private spaces

edges.why_related: sub routing is legal only where license attachment for sub work is verified for the jurisdiction
edges.risk_of_conflict: capacity pressure books sub crews before their credential coverage is confirmed

edges.why_related: monitored fire work proceeds only inside the credential class the jurisdiction permits the operation to hold
edges.risk_of_conflict: a life-safety upsell crosses into a reserved fire credential class

edges.why_related: signal testing must happen with the account on test so commissioning never becomes a false dispatch
edges.risk_of_conflict: an eager tech fires zone tests before the central station confirms test mode

edges.why_related: maximal coverage wants every angle; the charter forbids views into private spaces and neighbor property
edges.resolution_rule: the charter wins without exception: re-aim, mask, or delete the view, and refuse covert placements even when the paying customer insists

edges.why_related: raw sensitivity maximizes detection but multiplies false dispatches in fined and no-response jurisdictions
edges.resolution_rule: false-alarm exposure wins at the margin: prefer dual-tech, pet-rated, and confirmation-friendly configurations, and buy detection back with better placement rather than hotter settings

edges.why_related: piece-rate throughput rewards speed while the workmanship standard demands unpaid-looking care
edges.resolution_rule: the standard wins: sub volume is throttled to crews whose QC pass rate holds, pay is tied to passed inspections, and the checklist is never relaxed to protect a schedule

edges.why_related: budget trimming in the proposal pulls against the coverage the threat model says this home needs
edges.resolution_rule: trims must be visible and consented: declined coverage is recorded in the signed scope, life-safety and primary-entry perimeter are trimmed last, and no removal happens silently

edges.why_related: workmanship quality is the strongest controllable driver of early-life callback rates
device-class and placement choices largely determine the false-alarm callbacks a home generates
registration and permits complete before go-live so the first signals come from a legal, registered address
training follows a proven system; teaching on an untested panel rehearses failure
root-caused workmanship defects rewrite the checklist and retighten QC sampling
false-alarm clusters traced to placement or device class revise the placement rules for future designs
both close the job by transferring what was built - one verbally to the household, one as records to the office - and both erode first under end-of-day schedule pressure

conflict_axes.name: detection_coverage_vs_false_alarm_exposure
conflict_axes.description: More sensors at higher sensitivity catch more real events but multiply false dispatches, which fined and verified-response jurisdictions punish and which teach households to stop arming.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold perimeter coverage firm, spend the false-alarm budget on placement quality and dual-tech devices rather than hotter settings, and let the local ordinance posture set the margin

conflict_axes.name: camera_reach_vs_occupant_and_neighbor_privacy
conflict_axes.description: Wider, more numerous views see more of what matters and more of what is forbidden - neighbor property, private interior spaces, audio where consent rules bite.
poles: record only what is lawful and disclosed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the defensive charter dominates: masking, re-aiming, and refusal are the tools, and lost coverage is compensated on the customer's own property or not at all

conflict_axes.name: install_throughput_vs_workmanship_quality
conflict_axes.description: Sub crews and piece rates scale installed volume while every unit of speed pressure leans on the invisible workmanship the callback wave later invoices.
poles: hold every job to the QC standard
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tie pay and continued routing to passed QC, tighten sampling on new and slipping crews, and let volume - never the checklist - be the variable that gives

conflict_axes.name: wireless_speed_vs_hardwired_durability
conflict_axes.description: Wireless installs fast, forgives old construction, and suits retrofits; hardwired endures without battery service and shrugs off interference, but costs walls and hours.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the building decide: reuse sound existing wire, wireless where walls are precious or runs absurd, hybrid as the honest default, with battery-service load priced into wireless-heavy choices

conflict_axes.name: budget_trim_vs_threat_coverage
conflict_axes.description: The customer's number pulls the package down while the threat model's ranked entries demand devices; the danger zone is silent trimming that leaves both parties believing different systems were bought.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: trim visibly and in ranked order - convenience first, interior second, perimeter of primary entries and life-safety last - with every decline recorded in the signed scope

conflict_axes.name: takeover_reuse_vs_rip_and_replace
conflict_axes.description: Reusing legacy equipment saves labor and walls but inherits undocumented history; replacement costs more today and buys a known-good baseline the operation will service for years.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reuse only what passes a live test and speaks the platform's protocol; the panel usually goes, sound wire usually stays, and anything untestable is treated as absent

conflict_axes.name: ecosystem_standardization_vs_best_of_breed
conflict_axes.description: One platform across the install base compounds training, stock, and service efficiency; per-job best-of-breed picks the ideal device but fragments the operation into a museum of one-offs.
poles: the best device for each job
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: standardize the panel and communicator, allow best-of-breed only where the standard catalog genuinely cannot meet a surveyed need, and record every exception as service debt

conflict_axes.name: compliance_completeness_vs_schedule_pressure
conflict_axes.description: Permits, registrations, and verification steps sit between a signed customer and a mounted system, and every day of jurisdiction latency tempts the operation to drill first and file later.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compliance wins: the install calendar absorbs jurisdiction latency, customers are told the real timeline at signing, and no account goes live unregistered

conflict_axes.name: life_safety_ambition_vs_credential_reach
conflict_axes.description: Monitored smoke and CO are the highest-value add-ons in the catalog, and also the work most likely to cross into fire-code and credential territory the operation may not hold.
poles: stay strictly inside the credential class
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: verify the jurisdiction's fire-work rules before quoting, add listed monitored devices where clearly permitted, and refer out reserved work - a referred fire job costs a sale; an illegal one can cost the license

edge_cases.description: A multi-pet household where standard motions would trip nightly on animals crossing the rooms
edge_cases.trigger: the survey records dogs or cats with free run of spaces the plan wants motion coverage in
edge_cases.mitigation: pet-rated or dual-tech devices mounted out of the animals' plane of travel, aimed along human paths, with the pet reality noted per zone in the device schedule

edge_cases.description: The address sits in a verified-response jurisdiction where police ignore unverified burglar alarms
edge_cases.trigger: ordinance verification reveals a verified-response or chronically delayed-response policy
edge_cases.mitigation: design a verification means in - cameras covering likely entries or audio verification where lawful - and disclose to the customer in writing what response their city actually provides

edge_cases.description: The legacy panel is proprietary and its wireless sensors are encrypted to the incumbent vendor
edge_cases.trigger: the takeover assessment cannot enroll or even identify the existing sensors on any open protocol
edge_cases.mitigation: quote the honest rip-and-replace with the locked-ecosystem explanation in writing, salvaging only tested wire runs and mounts, and never promise takeover before the protocol check

edge_cases.description: No usable cellular signal at any interior panel location the home offers
edge_cases.trigger: the connectivity survey shows the communicator's primary path unusable where the panel must live
edge_cases.mitigation: relocate the panel within wire reach, add a high-gain antenna solution the platform supports, or re-architect around IP-primary with cellular elsewhere - and if no reliable path exists, say so before selling monitoring

edge_cases.description: The buyer asks for a concealed camera aimed at a caregiver, a tenant's room, or the neighbor's yard
edge_cases.trigger: any request for covert interior surveillance or off-property viewing during design
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse under the charter, offer the lawful alternative of disclosed cameras in common spaces and coverage of the customer's own approaches, and log the refusal with the alternative offered

edge_cases.description: A historic or rented home where drilling and wire-fishing are forbidden or destructive
edge_cases.trigger: plaster-and-lath construction, landlord no-modification terms, or preservation constraints surface at survey
edge_cases.mitigation: go wireless-first with surface mounts and removable adhesive standards, get the landlord's written permission where tenancy applies, and record the no-drill constraint in scope and QC expectations

edge_cases.description: A sub crew loses its qualifying credential holder mid-project
edge_cases.trigger: the person whose license covered the sub's work leaves or lapses while jobs are open
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the crew's open jobs immediately, verify what the jurisdiction allows during the gap, re-cover the work under a valid credential or reassign in-house, and re-inspect anything installed in the uncovered window

edge_cases.description: Commissioning zone tests dispatch police because the account was never placed on test
edge_cases.trigger: signal testing begins without central-station confirmation of test mode
edge_cases.mitigation: make on-test confirmation the first line of the commissioning log and a hard gate before any zone is tripped; after a slip, call the central station and authorities immediately and file the event as a process defect

edge_cases.description: A tenant wants a system in a landlord's property
edge_cases.trigger: the occupant contracting for the system does not own the walls it mounts to
edge_cases.mitigation: obtain the landlord's written consent for any penetration, bias the design to removable wireless, and state in the scope who owns the equipment and what restoration is promised at move-out

edge_cases.description: The customer wants monitored smoke detection in a jurisdiction that reserves fire-alarm work for a separate credential class
edge_cases.trigger: licensing verification flags fire work outside the operation's held credentials
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the reserved portion, refer it to a properly credentialed fire contractor, document the referral, and never quietly degrade or bypass the home's existing required detection

edge_cases.description: A new install generates a cluster of false alarms in its first month, drawing ordinance fines and threatening the address's response standing
edge_cases.trigger: repeated dispatches from one account shortly after handoff
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as an emergency root-cause: on-site within days, classify each event as user, placement, or hardware, retrain or re-place accordingly, and coordinate with the customer on the jurisdiction's fine and appeal process without paying it invisibly

workflow.action: Walk the property and write the survey
workflow.description: Record every opening, sightline, pet, household pattern, existing device, and panel candidate with photos
workflow.gate: every exterior door and reachable window is listed with construction type, pets and prior incidents noted, and panel/keypad candidates marked

workflow.action: Measure connectivity at the actual mount points
workflow.description: Take cellular readings at panel candidates and Wi-Fi measurements at each planned camera and doorbell position
workflow.gate: a usable communicator path exists at the chosen panel location and every camera position has measured bandwidth

workflow.action: Judge the existing system for takeover
workflow.description: Test and verdict every legacy component - keep, replace, or absent - against protocol compatibility and service life
workflow.gate: each legacy component carries a written keep/replace decision with test evidence, or none-present is recorded

workflow.description: Rank entry paths from survey evidence and fold in the household's stated concerns and constraints without exaggeration
workflow.gate: entry paths are ranked with survey evidence and every stated concern and constraint appears in the profile

workflow.description: Lay perimeter, interior, and 24-hour layers over the threat profile with named zones, partitions, and delay assignments
workflow.gate: every ranked entry path has a perimeter-layer device and only designated entry doors carry delay

workflow.action: Select the panel platform and communicator path
workflow.description: Commit to architecture, ecosystem, communicator, and panel placement justified by readings and the takeover verdict
workflow.gate: the chosen platform covers the zone plan's device needs and its communicator path is proven by the readings sheet

workflow.action: Specify detection and life-safety devices per zone
workflow.description: Fill each zone with the device class, mount position, and settings matched to construction, pets, and environment, with life-safety on supervised 24-hour zones
workflow.gate: each zone names its device class, position, and the surveyed condition that dictated it, and life-safety permissibility is verified

workflow.action: Plan camera and doorbell coverage with the privacy check
workflow.description: Sketch each field of view, decide mounting and power, apply masking, and verify bandwidth per camera
workflow.gate: every view passes the charter check, masking is noted where needed, and each camera's demand fits the measured connection

workflow.action: Write and sign the scope proposal
workflow.description: Put the bill of materials, labor scope, exclusions, change-order terms, capability limits, and any declined coverage in writing
workflow.artifact: signed scope and bill of materials
workflow.gate: the document contains no prevention or response guarantees and records every declined coverage with initials

workflow.action: Verify and complete permits and registration
workflow.description: Confirm current jurisdiction requirements from the authority, pull required permits, and register the alarm before go-live
workflow.gate: each obligation class shows either its permit/registration evidence or a dated, sourced not-required finding before install is scheduled

workflow.description: Execute the signed scope with concealed routing, sealed penetrations, labeled zones, and the photo QC checklist
workflow.gate: the punch list is empty and QC photos evidence every checklist item

workflow.description: With the account on test, walk-test every zone to received-at-monitoring confirmation, exercise both communicator paths and power loss, then run training and file the closeout package
workflow.artifact: commissioning log plus training sign-off and closeout package
workflow.gate: every zone shows a received confirmation, failover and battery behavior verified, each adult user demonstrated the core operations, and the record set is filed

dominance_rules.rule: The lawful-defensive charter dominates every design and sales consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: a single covert or neighbor-targeting installation exposes the operation to liability and forfeits the trust the whole trade runs on
dominance_rules.trigger: any device, view, or feature whose purpose is not defensive protection of the customer's own home
dominance_rules.action: refuse the placement, offer the lawful alternative, and log the refusal

dominance_rules.rule: Life-safety signal integrity dominates cost, convenience, and schedule
dominance_rules.rationale: a silenced or unsupervised smoke zone converts a design shortcut into a possible fatality
dominance_rules.trigger: any proposal to put life-safety on a disarmable zone, skip supervision, or defer its test
dominance_rules.action: block the shortcut; life-safety devices ride supervised 24-hour zones and are tested at commissioning without exception

dominance_rules.rule: Licensing and permit compliance dominates schedule pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: an unlicensed or unpermitted install is a legal exposure that no delivery date justifies
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed install date that precedes verified credentials, permits, or registration
dominance_rules.action: move the date, not the compliance step, and tell the customer the honest timeline

dominance_rules.rule: False-alarm prevention dominates raw sensitivity when the two collide
dominance_rules.rationale: false dispatches burn ordinance standing, fine the customer, and teach the household to disarm forever
dominance_rules.trigger: a configuration choice that buys detection margin at clear false-alarm cost in a fined or verified-response jurisdiction
dominance_rules.action: take the confirmation-friendly configuration and recover detection through placement and layering

dominance_rules.rule: The workmanship standard dominates subcontractor throughput
dominance_rules.rationale: volume installed below standard is not capacity, it is a callback debt with interest
dominance_rules.trigger: schedule or piece-rate pressure to relax QC, sampling, or the punch-list gate
dominance_rules.action: hold the gate and throttle routing to crews that pass; let volume slip before quality

dominance_rules.rule: Written honest scope dominates closing speed
dominance_rules.rationale: a signature won on prevention promises or silent trims becomes a fraud dispute after the first loss
dominance_rules.trigger: temptation to guarantee outcomes, omit exclusions, or trim coverage without recording it
dominance_rules.action: keep limits and declines in the signed document even if the deal cools

dominance_rules.rule: Perimeter coverage of primary entries dominates interior and convenience add-ons in any budget trim
dominance_rules.rationale: detection at the shell is the design's core promise; gadgets are negotiable, the back door is not
dominance_rules.trigger: a budget cut that would remove perimeter devices while convenience items survive
dominance_rules.action: re-order the trim so convenience goes first, interior second, primary-entry perimeter and life-safety last

dominance_rules.rule: Verified test evidence dominates installer self-report at every gate
dominance_rules.rationale: the zones that were never really tested are exactly the ones that fail during a real event
dominance_rules.trigger: a job presented as done whose log lacks per-zone received confirmations or QC photos
dominance_rules.action: reopen the job; no confirmation, no handoff

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete the survey and connectivity readings before selecting any platform or quoting any package
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mid-install platform swaps and dead-communicator discoveries after the panel is on the wall

anti_rework_rules.rule: Deliver the takeover verdict before the equipment quote
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-quoting the job and ripping out promised reuse when the legacy gear turns out locked or dead

anti_rework_rules.rule: Freeze the zone plan before ordering devices or scheduling crews
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wrong bills of materials, return trips for missing sensors, and improvised on-wall redesign

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify jurisdiction requirements and secure permits and registration before the install date is promised
anti_rework_rules.prevents: idle crews, failed inspections, and accounts going live unregistered into their first fine

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm signal readings at final mount points before any drilling
anti_rework_rules.prevents: relocating drilled devices and patching customer walls when the planned spot turns out deaf

anti_rework_rules.rule: Place the account on test with the central station before the first commissioning signal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: police dispatches to the install, ordinance fines, and a mortified customer on day one

anti_rework_rules.rule: Walk the customer through camera fields of view on the sketch before mounting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-install privacy disputes, neighbor complaints, and re-aim visits

anti_rework_rules.rule: Empty the QC punch list before scheduling training and handoff
anti_rework_rules.prevents: training sessions interrupted by tool bags reopening walls and repeat visits to finish what was called done

iteration_protocol.trigger: callbacks or false alarms cluster on a device class, placement pattern, or crew
iteration_protocol.action: root-cause the cluster, rewrite the implicated placement or workmanship rule, and re-inspect that crew's recent jobs

iteration_protocol.trigger: a served jurisdiction changes its licensing, permit, ordinance, or response policy
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the obligation map, update the design and registration defaults for that territory, and brief every crew working it

iteration_protocol.trigger: the platform vendor announces a sunset, catalog gap, or reliability trend on the standard stack
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the platform decision with current takeover and connectivity realities and plan the field-base migration deliberately

iteration_protocol.trigger: sub-crew QC or callback metrics diverge from in-house results
iteration_protocol.action: tighten sampling on the divergent crews, revisit piece-rate structure, and re-balance the sub-versus-in-house routing policy

iteration_protocol.trigger: commissioning failures recur on communicator paths or reused legacy components
iteration_protocol.action: audit the connectivity survey method and the takeover test bar, and raise whichever let the failures through

iteration_protocol.trigger: a privacy complaint, consent-law change, or charter-testing request pattern emerges
iteration_protocol.action: review installed views against the charter, update masking and refusal scripts, and retrain surveyors and designers on the boundary

iteration_protocol.trigger: change orders recur from survey-to-proposal gaps
iteration_protocol.action: diff the change-order causes against the survey checklist and extend it so the next survey captures what this one missed

priority_rationale: The frame nodes - the defensive charter, licensing awareness, and false-alarm ordinance posture - come first because they bound what may lawfully and wisely be designed at all; the survey trio (walk-through, connectivity, takeover) gathers the facts every later choice consumes; the design chain (threat model, zone plan, platform, sensors, cameras, life-safety) converts facts into a package the scope proposal freezes honestly; compliance paperwork and the capacity/vetting pair gate who installs and when; and the install-to-handoff sequence (workmanship, commissioning, training, closeout) proves the system before the callback loop turns field pain into better standards.
